transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Wu (Redwood AE), Marcus Lin (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Northstar Head of Platform), Derek Barnes (Northstar CTO), Aisha Mohammed (Northstar Security Lead)

[00:00] Evelyn: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro—I'm Evelyn, AE on the account, and Marcus is our SE who will dig into the networking. How are you all?
[00:07] Laura: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in, we have a few infra folks on, want to make sure Private deployment is feasible.
[00:12] Derek: Yep, hi. Quick context: we're a regulated finance platform, low latency reqs for realtime scoring, and strict data residency in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Trying to understand Redwood Private network options.
[00:22] Marcus: Great, thanks. I'll cover VPC connectivity, endpoints, and what we need for peering or PrivateLink. First question—are you thinking cross-account peering into our Redwood-managed VPC, or deploying Redwood's control plane inside your VPC? Or dedicated infra?
[00:35] Laura: We prefer customer-managed VPC where Redwood control plane sits in our AWS account, or at least private endpoints into our VPC. We don't want traffic egressing over public internet.
[00:44] Aisha: Security is main driver—SAML SSO, KMS for key management, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC2 reports. Also concerned about CIDR overlap with our existing network.
[00:55] Marcus: Totally reasonable. For Redwood Private we support two patterns: 1) Customer-managed deployment (we provide CloudFormation/Terraform to deploy Redwood in your VPC), or 2) Cross-account network connectivity where we host the infra in our account but expose PrivateLink endpoints or VPC peering. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:12] Derek: Can you expand on tradeoffs—esp cost and latency?
[01:16] Evelyn: Sure—customer-managed in your account gives you maximum control and eliminates egress charges to your infra; latency tends to be lower since it's in-region. Cross-account hosting with PrivateLink can be easier to get started, but sometimes introduces a small extra hop; also PrivateLink has per-GB charges on AWS.
[01:30] Marcus: For VPC peering—it's L3 routed peering. It's simple but requires non-overlapping CIDR ranges. PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) gives you endpoint svc connections, avoids route table changes, and works across accounts and VPCs, but requires NLBs and supports specific ports.
[01:46] Laura: We have a bunch of /16-ish ranges; overlap could be an issue. We'll need to do CIDR reconciliation. Can Redwood support e.g. NAT Gateway and shared services? We also use VPC endpoints for S3.
[01:58] Marcus: Yes—our deployment supports VPC endpoints for S3 and ECR. If you're deploying customer-managed, you control the NAT/IGW. If we host, we can set up PrivateLink endpoints into your VPC for API traffic and S3 gateway endpoints for object storage. Note, some customers prefer S3 interface endpoints vs gateway endpoints depending on account boundaries.
[02:15] Aisha: KMS—can you integrate with our CMKs? We cannot have keys controlled by a vendor.
[02:20] Marcus: We support customer-managed keys via cross-account grants to a Redwood service principal. For on-prem or fully air-gapped setups we have options to bring-your-own-HSM but that is a different path.
[02:30] Derek: Region constraints—we need instances in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Can Redwood run Private control planes in both regions? And do you replicate data between regions?
[02:39] Evelyn: Yes, we can deploy in both regions. For data residency, we ensure control plane and model caches can be pinned to a region. Replication is configurable—some state like audit logs can be forwarded to your central logging; model artifacts are pulled from your AMIs or S3 in-region.
[02:54] Laura: On networking, how do you handle egress IPs? We have allowlists for our internal services.
[02:58] Marcus: If customer-managed, your egress IPs are yours. If we host, we can assign Elastic IPs for egress or advise on NAT Gateway paths. We also can provide a list of expected CIDR ranges for inbound rules when using peering.
[03:10] Aisha: Audit logs—we want to ship everything to Splunk/Sumo via Kinesis/firehose, and keep 365 days for compliance.
[03:16] Marcus: We can forward logs to your logging endpoints; we support pushing to your Kinesis stream or using S3 buckets with lifecycle rules. We'll include CloudTrail and application logs; timestamps might be slightly off in transcriptions (not relevant), but we capture request/response latencies for tracing.
[03:33] Derek: What about performance—we need 2k rps for scoring with p50 latency <150ms. Is that feasible in Private?
[03:40] Marcus: Absolutely, with Dedicated GPU pools or customer-managed infra we'll size accordingly. Need to confirm average prompt lengths and KV-cache hit rates. We'll provide throughput estimates; Marcus: action—I'll model 2k rps with a few sequence-length profiles.
[03:56] Laura: Are there any known gotchas—like cross-region latency for KV cache, or serialization issues?
[04:02] Marcus: KV cache is local to inference nodes; cross-region calls add latency. If you pin traffic to a region, cache locality improves. Also, watch for TCP MSS and MTU with some NAT gateway setups—rare but seen.
[04:15] Evelyn: On compliance docs—I'll send our SOC2 pack and our private deployment checklist. Note sometimes transcription of product names is messy—our docs call it Redwood Private or Redwood Private VPC.
[04:27] Aisha: Good. Also we need RBAC integration with our Okta SAML; can you support SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:34] Marcus: Yes SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported. We also integrate with audit trail and can map roles to Redwood role sets.
[04:43] Derek: In terms of networking, we prefer peering if possible but worried about CIDR overlap. How do you recommend we approach resolving overlap?
[04:50] Marcus: Typical approach: 1) Export a list of allocated CIDRs per account/region, 2) We map necessary subnets for control plane and compute, 3) If overlap exists, use AWS PrivateLink or deploy Redwood into your account. We'll send a diagram.
[05:05] Laura: Awesome. Can you confirm the data flow for model artifacts? We prefer our model artifacts stored in our S3 with restricted access—Redwood should pull them from there.
[05:13] Marcus: Yes—customer-managed S3 with IAM roles is supported. For hosted variants, we can pull when given temp credentials but customer-managed is preferred for sensitive models.
[05:22] Evelyn: Pricing—high-level: hosted on public has pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity; Private has more integration work and a platform fee. We'll send a rough comparison.
[05:32] Derek: Any competitor notes—our infra team mentioned Anthropic and self-hosting; curious if you have references for finance customers.
[05:38] Evelyn: We can share references; will include 1-2 finance customers and a short benchmark sheet (latency/cost) for similar workloads.
[05:47] Laura: Sounds good. Next steps?
[05:50] Evelyn: We'll send: VPC peering vs PrivateLink diagram; SOC2 pack; KMS integration steps; and sizing/pricing for 2k rps. Also schedule a 1-hour infra deep-dive next week to finalize CIDRs—does 2026-05-25 work?
[06:05] Derek: Works for me.
[06:07] Aisha: Works.
[06:08] Evelyn: Great. Any final Qs? (pause)
[06:12] Laura: Not from me, thanks.
[06:14] Marcus: I'll start the sizing model and loop in our infra eng. Expect the packet by 2026-05-20.
[06:20] Evelyn: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and invite for the deep-dive. Bye.
[06:24] Derek: Thanks, bye.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (product names, e.g., 'PrivateLink' transcribed as 'Private Link' or 'Bedrocke' for Bedrock). Speaker labels are mostly correct; some crosstalk and interruptions.
